scope: Bounded primary-source research requested by user; no benchmark, install or runtime change yet.

sources.finding: CPython dictionaries use resizable hash tables; replacing them does not itself establish a point-lookup speedup.
Static C++ trie bindings offer compact storage, prefix operations and memory mapping. Published legacy benchmark numbers are not evidence for this taxonomy workload.
Indexed and covering-index queries can avoid full table scans and unnecessary table lookups.
SQLite supports memory-mapped database I/O with documented constraints and tradeoffs.

hypothesis: A prebuilt read-only indexed SQLite catalog plus bounded hot-record cache may improve cold startup and memory by loading relevant records lazily; in-memory dict point lookups may remain faster.
current_evidence: Saved profile attributes most repeated pipeline cost to strict codec/schema work; static metadata caching already improved 100 normalize+schema calls 6.052s to 2.890s. This is not a SQLite/trie comparison.
